## Observed Facts

Data Scope: Base Corpus, both Datasets, no filters. Counts are Log Entries, not incidents.

| Dataset | Log Entries | First timestamp | Last timestamp |
|---|---|---|---|
| BGL | 4,747,963 [E1] | 2005-06-03 15:42:50.363779 [E1] | 2006-01-04 08:00:05.233639 [E1] |
| OpenStack | 207,820 [E1] | 2017-05-14 19:39:01.445000 [E1] |  2017-05-17 12:02:35.320000 [E1] |

- BGL covers about seven months (June 2005 to early January 2006) [E1].
- OpenStack covers about three days (14 May to 17 May 2017) [E1].
- Combined, the Base Corpus holds 4,955,783 Log Entries [E1].

## Hypotheses

- BGL is the much larger Dataset by volume, so it will dominate any unfiltered count or trend. Compare the two Datasets separately when you report problem frequency.

## Unknowns

- The timestamps do not state a time zone, so I cannot say whether they are UTC or local time.
- The logs cannot show whether the Datasets have gaps inside their ranges. The min and max timestamps only bound the range; they do not show coverage density.
- The logs cannot tell me whether these two Datasets were sampled or are complete copies of their sources.

## Next Step

Run a per-week trend on BGL and on OpenStack (`mcp__logs__trend` with `bucket=week`) to see whether Log Entry volume is steady across the range or has spikes. Those spikes are the first place to look for recurring problems.
